title: The Milkmaid and Her Pail
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A farmer's daughter had been out to milk the cows, and was returning to the dairy carrying her pail of milk upon her head. As she walked along, she fell a-musing after this fashion: "The milk in this pail will provide me with cream, which I will make into butter and take to market to sell. With the money I will buy a number of eggs, and these, when hatched, will produce chickens, and by and by I shall have quite a large poultry-yard. Then I shall sell some of my fowls, and with the money which they will bring in I will buy myself a new gown, which I shall wear when I go to the fair; and all the young fellows will admire it, and come and make love to me, but I shall toss my head and have nothing to say to them." Forgetting all about the pail, and suiting the action to the word, she tossed her head. Down went the pail, all the milk was spilled, and all her fine castles in the air vanished in a moment!
Do not count your chickens before they are hatched.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how is the Milkmaid carrying her pail as she walks?
options: Under one arm
In both hands before her
Upon her head
Balanced on her shoulder

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Milkmaid plan to make from the cream in her pail?
options: Butter to take to market
Cheese to sell at the fair
A pudding for her family
A gift for the farmer

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Milkmaid plan to buy with the money from selling butter?
options: A new pail
A ticket to the fair
A flock of sheep
A number of eggs

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Milkmaid plan to buy once she sells her fowls?
options: A larger poultry-yard
A new gown to wear to the fair
A second pail for milking
A basket for carrying eggs

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Milkmaid imagine doing when young fellows admire her new gown?
options: Thanking each one of them warmly
Inviting them all to her poultry-yard
Tossing her head and having nothing to say to them
Asking them to help her sell more fowls

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens the moment the Milkmaid actually tosses her head?
options: Down goes the pail, and all the milk is spilled
She trips over a stone in the road
The cows begin to follow her home
She drops her basket of eggs

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Milkmaid end up spilling her milk?
options: The road is too uneven for her to walk safely
Another villager bumps into her without meaning to
The pail was already cracked before she set out
She acts out her daydream and forgets the pail balanced on her head

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the phrase "castles in the air" suggest about the Milkmaid's plans?
options: They were carefully written down before she set out
They were imaginary hopes that depended on nothing yet real
They were plans she had already carried out once before
They were promises made to her by the farmer

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Milkmaid "fell a-musing"?
options: She began singing a merry tune
She began arguing with herself
She began daydreaming to herself
She began walking more quickly

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: Don't count on rewards from a plan before it has actually succeeded
Milkmaids should never daydream while carrying a full pail
Selling butter is more profitable than selling eggs
New gowns are not worth saving money to buy

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where had the Milkmaid been just before the story begins?
options: Selling eggs at the market
Visiting the poultry-yard
Buying a new gown at the fair
Out milking the cows

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Milkmaid imagine her eggs will eventually produce?
options: A second pail of milk
Chickens, leading to a large poultry-yard
Enough cream for a whole season
A new flock of sheep

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Milkmaid plan to do with some of her fowls?
options: Give them away to neighbors
Keep them all for herself
Sell them for money
Trade them for a new pail

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Milkmaid's long chain of plans, from milk to gown, depend on the whole time?
options: A pail of milk that she has not yet even delivered
A promise already made to her by the farmer
Money she has already earned from selling eggs
A gown she has already bought at the fair

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Milkmaid's toss of the head matter so much to the story?
options: It is a signal to the young fellows that she admires them
It is meant to wake her from a nap
It causes the cows to wander off
It is the very action that spills the milk her whole plan relied on

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "vanished" mean in "her fine castles in the air vanished in a moment"?
options: Grew larger and clearer
Disappeared completely
Were written down for later
Were shared with someone else

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Milkmaid sells her milk and buys a new gown
A Milkmaid trades her pail for a basket of eggs
A Milkmaid loses her milk by acting out a daydream built on it
A Milkmaid's poultry-yard grows larger than she expected
